title: Insights Synthesizer for per-route/model/customer cost & latency
creator: Diego Alvarez
description:
Build a horizontally shardable backend service that synthesizes a clear, explainable breakdown of inference economics and latency per route, per served model variant, and per customer. The Insights Synthesizer ingests token-level usage events (generation start/end, model variant ID, sequence length, KV cache hit ratio), GPU execution traces (kernel durations, queue wait), billing records, and routing metadata. It produces daily and real-time aggregates surfaced to Console: per-route unit cost, model-specific latency distributions (p50/p95/p99), attribution of shared overhead (e.g., batching and routing tax), and suggested optimizations (e.g., switch to quantized variant, increase batch cap) with delta estimates.

Scope and constraints: service must be multi-tenant-safe, support per-customer partitioning for Dedicated/Private accounts, tolerate delayed billing ingestion, and be resilient to upstream schema changes. Must run both a streaming fast-path for near-real-time spending alerts and a batch reconciliation pass for canonical ledgers. We will favor deterministic, explainable attribution heuristics over opaque ML models so product teams can reason about recommendations.

Key technical approach: 1) Canonicalize incoming events into a compact event envelope with stable fields (route_id, model_id, variant, customer_id, tokens_in/tokens_out, start_ts, end_ts, batch_id, kv_hit_count). 2) Use a combination of stateful stream processors (for fast-path) and a daily Spark/Beam job (for authoritative rollups). 3) Attribution algorithm: allocate shared GPU time to requests by normalized effective-token-weight (tokens * kernel-cost-factor) after subtracting prefix-cached savings; route-level fixed costs (e.g., network egress, orchestration) are apportioned by long-window traffic share. 4) Compute latency decomposition: queue wait, dispatch, kernel exec, serialization, and network I/O. 5) Store final artifacts as time-partitioned materialized tables and a compact JSON explanation per (route,model,customer,day) for Console to display and for API consumers.

Operational notes: will expose a read API for Console and an internal bulk export job for chargeback. Sharding key will be customer_id primary, with route_id as secondary bucketing to avoid hotspots from high-frequency routes. Include incremental reconciliation to replay late events and a diff/patch mechanism to update previously published daily artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming fast-path produces per-route per-model per-customer estimates with <= 5% error vs batch nightly ledger for small tenants
Nightly batch job produces canonical daily artifacts and a JSON explanation object stored in materialized table
Console can query the service API and surface cost and latency breakdown with explanation text and top-3 optimization suggestions
Service supports replay of late events and applies diffs to persisted artifacts with audit log entries
Load test: service sustains synthetic peak of 50k events/sec with 95th percentile latency under 2s on streaming paths
progress_updates: 2026-01-26 - Kickoff: aligned on dual-path architecture (streaming + batch). Owners: Priya (service), Anil (stream processors), Mei (batch).
2026-02-02 - Prototype: implemented event canonicalizer and small local runner for attribution heuristics. Observed edge cases around variant name normalization.

2026-02-18 - Design review: reviewed proposed attribution formula with PM and Finance (link: https://redwood-internal/docs/console-telemetry/insights-synthesizer). Decision: use effective-token-weight and subtract prefix cache savings before allocation.
2026-02-24 - Infra sync: reserved Kafka topic + added consumer groups for customer sharding. Added schema evolution tests to CI.
2026-03-03 - PR opened for streaming processors (github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/492). Initial benchmarks show 40k events/sec on c5n.2xlarge-equivalent test nodes.
2026-03-09 - QA: started integration test with billing ledger, discovered timestamp drift causing late attribution; added watermark policy and a late-event buffer implementation.
decisions: Prefer deterministic rule-based attribution to keep recommendations explainable to customers and auditors.
Primary sharding key is customer_id to enforce tenant isolation; route-level bucketing inside customer shard prevents heavy routes from causing cross-tenant impact.
Expose both near-real-time estimates and nightly canonical artifacts; nightly artifacts are the source-of-truth for billing/chargeback.
Keep explanation objects compact (max 4KB) and store them alongside daily rollups for Console to fetch without extra joins.
